subject: Clarify SOC 2 Type II coverage end-date semantics and bridge letter next steps
body:
From: Elizabeth Meyer <elizabeth.meyer@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: pwc-security@pwc.com
Date: Mon, 30 Sep 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 coverage question — end date semantics

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for sending the SOC 2 Type II report summary. A couple quick clarifying questions from our security team:

1) The report lists the period as '2028-01-01 through 2028-06-30'. Can you confirm whether the end date is inclusive (i.e., up to 23:59:59 on 2028-06-30) or if it should be interpreted as 'through the start of 2028-06-30'? Our SOC checklist specifically asks whether 'through' includes the full final day.

2) We have a scheduled data migration that completed on 2028-07-01 02:10 UTC. For audit purposes the auditor may request a bridge letter for 2028-07-01. Would Redwood be able to provide a bridge letter confirming controls coverage for the migration window and the immediate cutover?

3) If bridge letter is possible, what evidence (log exports, manifest, signed statement) do you typically include — and what's the expected lead time?

Appreciate the quick clarification — PwC is on the thread.

Thanks,
Elizabeth Meyer
Sr. Security Program Manager
Acme Corp

-----Original Message attached: redwood_soc2_summary_2028-06.pdf (pdf, 320KB)-----

---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elizabeth Meyer <elizabeth.meyer@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, PwC SOC Team <pwc-security@pwc.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Sep 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question — end date semantics

Hi Elizabeth — great questions. Short answers up front: 1) 'Through 2028-06-30' is inclusive of the entire calendar day (we treat the day as up to 23:59:59 UTC for evidence capture). 2) Yes, we can provide a bridge letter covering the immediate migration/cutover window. 3) Typical evidence set is a signed bridge letter, an evidence manifest (log export slices and retention statements), and a short summary from our infra team.

Im looping in Karthik (audit lead) to confirm the wording and Neha to prepare a draft bridge letter and the evidence manifest.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik confirms that inclusive semantics are consistent with our auditor's interpretation.
- Neha shares a draft bridge letter + manifest for Acme to review by EOD tomorrow.
- If PwC needs additional artifacts (sample logs, runbook excerpt), call them out and well schedule a 30-min sync.

Attaching the one-page SOC 2 summary again for quick reference.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary_2028-06.pdf

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Elizabeth Meyer <elizabeth.meyer@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, PwC SOC Team <pwc-security@pwc.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Sep 2029 12:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question — end date semantics

Thanks Vanessa / Elizabeth. Confirming from an auditor-facing perspective: when we state the coverage as 'through 2028-06-30' our Type II testing and evidence collection span the full UTC day ending 2028-06-30T23:59:59Z. Where there are short operational windows (e.g., migrations) that fall immediately after the reporting period, auditors commonly request a bridge letter that:

- Describes the event, the precise window of operational impact, and the controls in place during that window;
- Indicates whether there were any known control exceptions; and
- Attaches an evidence manifest with exported logs (time-sliced), retention policy statements, and a contact for follow-up.

We can sign a bridge letter that is explicit about the 2028-07-01 migration window and state that controls described in the Type II report remained in effect during the migration. Typical lead time for a draft is 24-48 business hours (depending on evidence availability) and turnaround for a signed DocuSign package is ~2 business days.

Ill ask Neha to start the manifest and draft. Elizabeth/PwC: if you have a preferred template or mandatory language for your artifact, drop it here and well incorporate it.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Compliance Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Elizabeth Meyer <elizabeth.meyer@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, PwC SOC Team <pwc-security@pwc.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Oct 2029 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft bridge letter + evidence manifest for Acme (attached)

Hi all,

Please find attached a first draft of the bridge letter and the evidence manifest. Summary of whats included:

- bridge_letter_draft_v1.docx: formal statement confirming controls in effect for the migration window (2028-07-01 00:00 UTC through 2028-07-01 04:00 UTC) and stating no detected control exceptions during that window based on available logs;
- evidence_manifest_2028-06.csv: manifest listing exported log slices (auth events, deployment runbook entries, KV cache snapshots) with start/end times and S3 object paths;
- redwood_soc2_summary_2028-06.pdf: one-page summary of the Type II scope (attached again for convenience).

Notes / asks:
- PwC: please confirm whether the wording 'no detected control exceptions based on available logs' is acceptable, or if you require stronger auditor-verified language.
- Elizabeth / Acme: please confirm the migration window described above matches your internal timestamp (you mentioned 2028-07-01 02:10 UTC — we included a conservative 00:00-04:00 UTC window).
- Vanessa: we can produce the full sample logs (redacted) if PwC asks — lead time for exports ~48 hours.

Attachments: bridge_letter_draft_v1.docx, evidence_manifest_2028-06.csv, redwood_soc2_summary_2028-06.pdf

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Compliance Program Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Draft bridge letter + evidence manifest for Acme (attached)

Neha — thanks, this looks good and the window matches our internal records; 00:00-04:00 UTC is fine. Two quick requests:

1) Could you add the manual rollback checklist excerpt to the manifest (we only need the runbook IDs and timestamps, not the full runbook content)? Thats something our auditor typically checks.
2) For the phrase 'no detected control exceptions based on available logs' — PwC, can you confirm that note is acceptable for a vendor bridge letter? If not, what alternative phrasing do you need?

If PwC is happy, were ready to proceed with DocuSign.

Thanks,
Elizabeth
